turns.t: We were told to come back today. The midwife said the baby was a bit yellow on Tuesday.
Yes, I've got the note. Come in, sit down. I'm Dr Shah. And you are? ~
Elena, I'm Sofia's mum. She's five days old now. ~
Hello, I'm Marsha, the healthcare assistant. I did her bilirubin reading just before you came in.
Thank you, Marsha. Elena, tell me how she's been since the midwife saw her. ~
She's been sleepy, very sleepy, I have to wake her for feeds. And she's not finishing them, she falls asleep on the breast.
How many feeds is she taking in a day, roughly?
Six or seven, but short ones. I'm not sure it's enough.
Waaah. ~
She's telling us she's hungry. When did you first notice the yellow colour?
I couldn't tell you exactly. Maybe Monday, maybe Tuesday morning, I honestly don't know. I'm not good at remembering with so little sleep.
That's absolutely fine. Are her nappies wet and what colour are her poos?
Wet, plenty. The poos are yellow-green, not pale. I looked at them in the light, like they said.
Good. Has she had any fevers or felt hot?
No, nothing hot. She's actually a bit cool, with her little hands.
How was the birth? Was she born on time?
Thirty-seven weeks, so a bit early, but she was a good weight.
Doctor, the reading I got was 210. I did it twice.
Thanks, Marsha. Let me weigh and measure her.
Heart rate 142, temperature 36.9, breathing rate 38, oxygen 98 percent, weight 3.1 kilos.
Is she losing weight? ~
She's a little under her birth weight, which is common at this stage, but I'd like to keep a close eye. ~
Waaah. ~
I'll examine her. Marsha, would you hold her head? ~
Yes, doctor.
She's yellow down to her chest, her soft spot is flat and normal, and she's alert when she's awake, with good tone.
Is that bad, the yellow? ~
Many newborns get jaundice, and it's usually harmless. But at five days, with the sleepiness and the reading Marsha took, I want to check it with a blood test. ~
A blood test on a baby? ~
It's a heel prick, just a few drops. I'd like to send a bilirubin blood test today, and I'd like her feed volumes checked with the midwife.
I'll book the heel prick now. ~
What do I do for her, meantime? ~
Feed her at least eight times a day, wake her if she sleeps more than three hours, and keep her in daylight, near a window, not in direct sun.
Okay. And if she gets more yellow? ~
If she's very sleepy, won't feed, or her poos go pale, ring us straight away, any hour.
I will. ~
And I'd like to see you both tomorrow, to review the result and her weight.
Tomorrow. Thank you, doctor. ~

chief_complaint.value: the baby was a bit yellow on Tuesday

physical_examination.finding: soft spot is flat and normal

clinical_uncertainties.description: Mother could not say when the yellow colour first appeared ("maybe Monday, maybe Tuesday morning").

clinical_actions.description: Feed at least eight times a day, wake after three hours, keep near daylight
Safety-net: ring if very sleepy, not feeding or pale stools
